items.summary: Retain the canonical allthingsmasonic.com affiliate CTA experiment after one delivery slot is released. Evidence: 61 Amazon clicks, 0 ordered items, and $0 site-attributed commission for 2026-09-21; this is a baseline, not causal proof. Test only CTA hierarchy, destination clarity, adjacent disclosure, keyboard focus, and mobile layout. Metric: site Amazon clicks, with orders and commission observed only if available. Learn in 14 days or 100 relevant new impressions/clicks; rollback the single diff if validation fails. Defer all new CRO prototypes while capacity is 10/10 and 57 improvements remain in measurement.

Three repository signals are research leads, not adoption approvals. MarkItDown (MIT; lab 8/8 bounded checks) could support a disposable SEO/content pipeline that converts approved source documents into structured drafts, metadata candidates, and internal-link suggestions. Smallest prototype: process 10 non-production documents, compare outputs against a fixed human rubric, and measure valid suggestions per document and review minutes saved. Risks: parser coverage, malformed or adversarial inputs, dependency maintenance, and no demonstrated fleet ROI. shadcn/ui (MIT; 3/3 lab checks) could support an accessible CTA component prototype; measure keyboard/accessibility defects and implementation time, with supply-chain and framework-compatibility review. Mermaid (MIT; no native checks available) could support explanatory diagrams in high-intent guides; prototype one static diagram and measure comprehension or CTA progression only if existing telemetry supports it. Keep all prototypes disposable, dependency-free in the CRO lab, non-production, and capacity-gated.
